title: Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

reading.body:
This is a case of a deployed tool carrying hidden logic that its users could not see. The markers were embedded in the system prompt Claude Code sends to the model, and they triggered on environment signals: the configured API base URL and the machine's timezone. The behaviour changed silently depending on where the tool was run and which endpoint it was pointed at, so the same product produced different output for different users without telling them.

The failure mode is a system used outside the conditions it was built for, or more precisely a system whose operators concealed the conditions under which it behaves differently. Catching it required reading the shipped binary rather than the documentation, since the domain and keyword lists were obfuscated as base64 strings behind an XOR key. A normal user had no way to observe the switch, and the reporting notes the marker was easy to bypass and left most users unaffected.

What is not established is Anthropic's intent. The company described the mechanism as an experiment, and that characterisation is a statement by the company rather than an independent finding. The reported consequence at Alibaba, a workplace ban over alleged backdoor risks, rests on a source account and an allegation, not on a verified security assessment.

reports.title: Claude Code Is Steganographically Marking Requests
Anthropic is removing its covert code for catching Chinese competitors
Claude Code’s hidden tracker was an “experiment,” says Anthropic
Alibaba to ban employees from using Anthropic's coding tool, source says

summary:
A blog post reports that Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent, hides markers in the system prompt it sends to the model. The code checks the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL setting and the system timezone. If the timezone is Asia/Shanghai or Asia/Urumqi, the date format changes from hyphens to slashes. If the API hostname matches a hidden list of domains or AI lab keywords, the apostrophe in the date sentence is swapped for a different Unicode character. The domain and keyword lists are stored as base64 strings and decoded with an XOR key.

The author inspected version 2.1.196 and found the binary signed by Anthropic. On their machine, with no base URL set and a Hong Kong timezone, the normal output appears. The article says the feature likely targets resellers, unauthorized gateways, and distillation pipelines, but calls the hidden approach a strange choice for a tool that asks for trust. It notes the marker is easy to bypass and that most normal users are unaffected.
